bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html used a regular expression that did not consume attacker-controlled HTML tags containing line terminators. For example, <img\nsrc=x\nonerror=alert(1)> survives the filter, while a browser treats the newlines as attribute whitespace and executes the event handler when the rendered result is inserted as HTML, enabling stored or reflected XSS in applications that rely on strip_html as a sanitizer.
flaw_origin: The vulnerability began when 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 first added strip_html using /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g. That implementation only removed simple attribute-free tags, so the advisory payload with newline-separated attributes already survived. Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 later replaced it with the Ruby-Liquid-style alternatives including <.*?>; this is the exact dot-does-not-match-line-terminators mechanism described by the advisory, but it is not the causal BIC because the same payload also survives its parent. Commit 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205 made script, style, and comment alternatives multiline-aware with [\s\S] while leaving the generic <.*?> branch vulnerable. Refactors and moves through 2024 preserved that branch.
ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2` shows author and committer `harttle <yangjvn@126.com>`, message `filters: all`, and no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: Bundle advisory GHSA-2qv6-9wx5-cwv4 / CVE-2026-44644 identifies src/filters/html.ts, vulnerable versions <= 10.25.7, fix reference 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045, and release v10.26.0.

`git show --format=raw 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 -- filters.js` shows this single-parent commit adding `liquid.registerFilter('strip_html', v => _.replace(v, /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g, ''))`; the raw header names parent b478c798fdd5aba96b1fa279dd78410d4844584c.
`git show b478c798fdd5aba96b1fa279dd78410d4844584c:filters.js` directly verifies the parent registers only abs through escape_once and contains no strip_html filter or vulnerable regex.

A Node reproduction applying the historical regexes to `<img\nsrc=x\nonerror=alert(1)>` prints the payload unchanged for the 4595e287 regex, the 8e9e10 regex, and the later regex with multiline script/style/comment alternatives, but prints an empty string for the fixed generic alternative `<[\s\S]*?>`.

`git blame -L 70,74 677e8511e60a7cc789dd33a4f295a46beeaf1137^ -- src/filters.js` attributes the vulnerable Ruby-Liquid-style `<.*?>` line to 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887. `git show 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887` shows it changed the older, already bypassable simple-tag regex rather than first creating the attack path. `git log -L '/export function strip_html/,/^}/':src/filters/html.ts` traces the preserved catch-all through the later moves/refactors and the final change.
`git show 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205` changes script/style/comment alternatives from dot to [\s\S] but keeps `<.*?>`, demonstrating why generic multiline tags remained exploitable.

`git show b976669ad3b21ad37c8aa2af3ef5709e2a58fe35` is the direct branch fix: it changes only the generic alternative from `<.*?>` to `<[\s\S]*?>` and adds img/svg newline and carriage-return regression cases. Its commit message includes `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>`, but protocol excludes fix-only AI evidence from the BIC judgment.

`git show 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045` shows the same security patch landed on the mainline as squash commit `fix: strip html newline tags (#892)`; therefore 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 is fix_sha and reconstructable member b976669ad3b21ad37c8aa2af3ef5709e2a58fe35 is direct_fix_sha.

`git tag --contains 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 | sort -V` begins with v1.2.0, establishing the first tagged affected release in this clone. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 v10.25.7` exits 1, while the same command for v10.26.0 exits 0; `git tag --contains 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 | sort -V` begins with v10.26.0.
`git cat-file commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2` is the BIC-only AI check and contains a human author/committer, the one-line message `filters: all`, and no trailers or bot marker.
reasoning: The smallest causal boundary is the original strip_html addition in 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2: its immediate parent has no such filter, while the added regex passes the advisory's executable multiline img payload. The visually closer 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 commit first wrote `<.*?>`, but cannot be the BIC because direct execution shows its parent already passes the same payload; it merely changed the flawed regex mechanism. The vulnerability then persisted continuously until direct member b976669ad3b21ad37c8aa2af3ef5709e2a58fe35 made the generic tag alternative line-terminator-aware and squash commit 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 landed it for v10.26.0. The true BIC predates contemporary coding-agent use and its commit object has no AI identity or marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI; Cursor attribution on the later fix is deliberately irrelevant.
